Hill also cited the need for improvement in sportswear and the Jordan brand.

Hill rejoined Nike as CEO in October 2024 as the company sought a pivot due to problems that included an oversupply of too many items that sold poorly and an ill-conceived shift to direct sales that left the company underrepresented with key retailers.
Hill told analysts the company has made progress since his return, but that deeper changes were needed following a comprehensive review.
Nike "must make changes to become a more agile, efficient and athlete-focused company," Hill said in a message to employees.
These shifts "will result in fewer roles across Nike, and I want to acknowledge that news like this creates uncertainty," said Hill, who promised "transparency" as the plans become clearer.
"Decisions about impacted roles related to this work will begin in calendar year 2027 and beyond," Hill said.

Nike plans a new campus in Bengaluru, India, which will represent "a long-term investment in new capabilities and talent to strengthen how we serve athletes around the world, including in India," Hill said in the message.
Neil Saunders, managing director of GlobalData, said the latest results show "Nike's brand heat continues to fade and it isn't powerful enough to punch back against more nimble competitors."
The company's forecast for a further decline in revenues was particularly troubling, said Saunders, who called the outlook "shabby."
Shares of Nike tumbled 7.1 per cent in after-hours trading.--AFP
0018d25c18a4a3d9: WASHINGTON: The Pentagon may soon deploy an additional aircraft carrier and 10,000 sailors and Marines to the Persian Gulf, according to a US official, a move that gives US commanders more options if president Donald Trump chooses to escalate attacks on Iran.

The USS Theodore Roosevelt carrier left its San Diego home port on Sunday, the official said, adding that no final decision on its destination had been made and that it gives US Central Command more options in the region.

If the Roosevelt does arrive in the Middle East, it will bring the number of carrier strike groups in the region back up to three, the same number as at the outset of the war against Iran. It would also bring to the region the carrier’s 5,000 sailors and Marines and thousands of others spread across its accompanying vessels.
The carrier movements come as Trump said increased military strikes against Iran were “possible” after the November midterm elections.

The USS George HW Bush and the USS George Washington will remain in the region. Before the 2026 operations against Iran, the last time the US had three carrier strike groups in the Middle East was in 2003, when they supported the early phase of the invasion of Iraq.
US Central Command, which oversees military operations in the Middle East, said in a statement that “we don’t discuss unit schedules for operational security reasons.”

On Monday, the USS Makin Island amphibious readiness group - with an assault ship, aircraft and 2,200 Marines - also set sail, giving Centcom additional options, the US official said. The USS Boxer amphibious readiness group is currently conducting operations near the Strait of Hormuz.
Deploying three aircraft carriers risks exacerbating the Navy’s current readiness woes, according to Ronald O’Rourke, a long-time analyst of naval forces.

The strain on the service was underscored by the controversial extended deployments of the USS Abraham Lincoln, which arrived in Thailand last month after a nine-month tour, and the USS Gerald Ford, which was dispatched to the Mideast after supporting operations against Venezuela and was at sea for 11 months.

“Maintaining even a two-carrier presence in that area over an extended period of time would be a strain for the carrier force,” said O’Rourke, an expert who retired from the Congressional Research Service. But “maintaining a three-carrier presence in that area for an extended period would be a significantly greater strain.”

There’s been a lull in major US or Iranian military strikes amid efforts to rekindle diplomatic negotiations. However, talks to end the war - now in its eighth month - remain deadlocked over issues including Tehran’s control of the Strait of Hormuz.
Iran’s foreign minister Abbas Araghchi has suggested in private talks recently that Tehran was willing to restore nuclear inspectors’ access to bombed facilities in exchange for sanctions relief.
f2c123811b166b4c: KUALA LUMPUR: Prolonged exposure to fine particulate matter (PM2.5) can pose serious health risks beyond respiratory problems, particularly among vulnerable groups.

Malaysian Environmental Health Practitioners Association chairman Prof Dr Jamal Hisham Hashim said a 2024 study in The Lancet Planetary Health found that about a million premature deaths globally each year were attributable to short-term exposure to PM2.5 lasting several hours to days.
He said PM2.5, produced by combustion processes, was small enough to penetrate deep into the lungs and reach the alveolar region where gas exchange occurs.
"This represents 2.08 per cent of the total annual global deaths between 2000 and 2019.
"The country with the higher percentage of global deaths attributable to PM2.5 was China with 3.2 per cent of global deaths in 2019."
Dr Jamal said prolonged exposure was particularly concerning for vulnerable groups, including children, the elderly and people with chronic respiratory and cardiovascular conditions.
These include those with asthma, rhinitis, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease (COPD), hypertension, ischaemic heart disease and diabetes.

Meanwhile, Academy of Occupational and Environmental Medicine Malaysia president Dr Abu Hasan Samad said outdoor workers faced greater exposure to haze as physical activity could cause them to breathe more frequently and deeply.
He said this could also place additional strain on the heart, particularly among older workers and those with existing conditions.
Dr Abu said employers should have interim measures in place during prolonged haze episodes.

He said unhealthy Air Pollutant Index levels should prompt employers to reduce strenuous outdoor work and working hours, provide more frequent breaks, ensure workers are equipped with appropriate respiratory protection and encourage sufficient hydration.
He said vulnerable workers should be assigned to indoor duties where possible.
"They should not be allowed to return to work without proper protection, work adjustment and supervision."
If unhealthy air quality persisted this month, Dr Abu said the Human Resources and Health ministries should issue guidance for workplaces, including provisions for working from home.

"Some form of financial assistance may have to be extended to the affected workers who can no longer earn a reasonable income due to prolonged or more severe haze, more so for the informal and gig workers."
69a3bee954a73bda: KUALA LUMPUR: The National Lung Health Initiative (NLHI) was launched in February 2025 as a targeted effort to tackle late-stage lung cancer diagnoses in Malaysia, but has since grown into something much bigger.

According to Dr Nor Aryana Hassan, director of the health ministry's disease control division, addressing lung cancer, one of the most common cancers among Malaysian men, was the starting point for what has become one of the country's most ambitious health reforms.
"When we started discussions, we found that the lung health initiative was not merely about lung cancer. It's actually beyond that."
Rather than running separate programmes for individual pulmonary conditions, the ministry began consolidating them into a single framework centered on overall lung health.
Integrating Malaysia’s lung-health efforts

Dr M Murallitharan, managing director of the National Cancer Society Malaysia (NCSM), a collaborator in the initiative, said the goal was to bring Malaysia’s fragmented approach to lung health under one roof.

"We're using NLHI as one strategy to unite our different health systems, as well as entities outside the health system, to work together in improving our health as a whole, using the lung as a focal point."

NLHI now brings together lung cancer, chronic obstructive pulmonary disease, asthma and tuberculosis under a single national framework, built around the idea that these diseases, while clinically distinct, share overlapping risk factors such as smoking, occupational exposure and air pollution.
The overlapping risk factors highlight the need for a broader approach to prevention.
"When we talk more about primary prevention, it’s actually beyond the health ministry’s role alone," Aryana said.
Rather than creating parallel, disconnected programmes, the health ministry gathered strategic plans from partner agencies and folded them into the lung-health framework.
Within Malaysia, the framework spans prevention, screening, diagnosis, treatment and long-term care, delivered through public and private clinics, high-risk workplaces and community outreach.
Its best-known initiative is LungShield, a screening scheme that combines an AI-assisted chest X-ray with micro-insurance to cover follow-up tests.
Addressing barriers
Beyond physical access, there are also internal mindset barriers to screening, said Murallitharan.
"We believe in our own health to a point that we don’t think that any kind of assessment is necessary. That is still the greatest barrier, the self kind of appraisal."
But even among those willing to be screened, the costs and accessibility of follow-up diagnostic tests can prevent them from going further.
LungShield, developed by NCSM and insurer MCIS Life, is designed to bridge that gap.
"If the X-ray picks up something, the insurance pays for everything up to molecular testing and staging," Murallitharan said.
Participants pay RM179 under a promotional rate, or RM479 at the standard corporate rate, and NCSM uses the difference to cross-subsidise screening in rural and lower-income communities.
Replicability of NLHI across Asean

Malaysia is now looking to extend elements of the NLHI across the region, with the proposal raised at a side event at the 17th Asean Health Ministers’ Meeting in Kuala Lumpur and formally included in the newly endorsed Asean Strategic Health Agenda 2026-2030.

Aryana said the next step would be to develop a strategic plan outlining how each member state can build on its existing lung-health programmes, followed by the development of an Asean guideline, based on information gathered from each country's activities and systems.

Murallitharan, however, said regional adoption did not necessarily mean that every country had to build the same system from scratch. Instead, elements of the Malaysian model could be adapted to local healthcare systems and markets, he said.
LungShield, for example, could be introduced through insurers that already operate across several Asean countries, he added.
He said Malaysia negotiated pricing with the technology provider on behalf of the region, rather than solely for the Malaysian market.
He added that other countries could use Malaysia’s negotiated rate, describing this as an example of the region’s "neighbourly spirit".
450990892673f54d: KUALA LUMPUR: Inisiatif Kesihatan Paru-paru Kebangsaan (NLHI) pada asalnya dilancarkan untuk menangani kelewatan diagnosis kanser itu, kini diperluas sebagai model menyeluruh kesihatan paru-paru yang berpotensi diguna pakai di Asean.
NLHI dilancarkan pada Februari 2025 dengan tumpuan awal terhadap kanser paru-paru, antara paling lazim dalam kalangan lelaki Malaysia.
Menurut Pengarah Bahagian Kawalan Penyakit Kementerian Kesihatan (KKM), Dr Nor Aryana Hassan, skop inisiatif itu kini jauh lebih luas.
"Apabila kami mula berbincang, kami mendapati inisiatif kesihatan paru-paru ini bukan sekadar mengenai kanser paru-paru. Ia sebenarnya lebih daripada itu," katanya.
Daripada menjalankan program berasingan mengikut penyakit, KKM menggabungkan usaha berkaitan di bawah satu kerangka yang memberi tumpuan kepada kesihatan paru-paru secara menyeluruh.
Satukan usaha kesihatan paru-paru
Pengarah Urusan Persatuan Kanser Kebangsaan Malaysia (NCSM), Dr M Murallitharan, berkata NLHI bertujuan menyatukan usaha kesihatan paru-paru yang sebelum ini dilaksanakan secara berasingan.

"Kami menggunakan NLHI sebagai satu strategi untuk menyatukan sistem kesihatan kita, serta entiti di luar sistem kesihatan, supaya dapat bekerjasama meningkatkan kesihatan secara keseluruhan, dengan paru-paru sebagai fokus," katanya.
NLHI kini merangkumi kanser paru-paru, penyakit pulmonari obstruktif kronik (COPD), asma dan tuberkulosis.
Penyakit itu berbeza dari segi klinikal, tetapi berkongsi faktor risiko seperti merokok, pendedahan di tempat kerja dan pencemaran udara.
Menurut Aryana, faktor risiko yang bertindih menunjukkan pencegahan tidak boleh hanya bergantung kepada KKM.
“Apabila kita bercakap mengenai pencegahan primer, ia sebenarnya melangkaui peranan KKM,” katanya.
Kerangka itu merangkumi pencegahan, saringan, diagnosis, rawatan dan penjagaan jangka panjang melalui klinik awam dan swasta, tempat kerja berisiko tinggi serta program komuniti.
Program paling dikenali bawah NLHI ialah LungShield, yang menggabungkan saringan X-ray dada dibantu kecerdasan buatan (AI) dengan insurans mikro bagi menampung kos ujian susulan.
Menangani halangan
Murallitharan berkata, sikap orang ramai terhadap pemeriksaan kesihatan turut menjadi cabaran.
“Kita begitu yakin dengan kesihatan sendiri sehingga tidak fikir sebarang pemeriksaan diperlukan. Itu masih menjadi halangan terbesar, iaitu penilaian terhadap diri sendiri," katanya.
Bagi mereka yang mahu menjalani saringan pula, kos dan akses kepada ujian susulan boleh menjadi penghalang.
LungShield, yang dibangunkan NCSM bersama MCIS Life, cuba menutup jurang itu.
“Jika X-ray mengesan sesuatu, insurans akan menanggung semuanya sehingga ujian molekul dan penentuan tahap penyakit,” katanya.
Peserta membayar RM179 pada kadar promosi atau RM479 pada kadar korporat standard.
NCSM menggunakan perbezaan itu untuk memberi subsidi silang bagi saringan di kawasan luar bandar dan komuniti berpendapatan rendah.
Potensi model kepada Asean
Malaysia kini mahu memperluas beberapa elemen NLHI ke peringkat serantau.

Cadangan itu dibincangkan pada acara sampingan Mesyuarat Menteri-menteri Kesihatan Asean ke-17 di Kuala Lumpur dan kemudian dimasukkan dalam Agenda Kesihatan Strategik Asean (ASHA) 2026-2030 yang baru diluluskan.
Aryana berkata, langkah seterusnya ialah membangunkan pelan strategik berdasarkan program kesihatan paru-paru sedia ada di setiap negara anggota, sebelum garis panduan Asean dibentuk.

Namun, Murallitharan berkata negara Asean tidak perlu meniru keseluruhan model Malaysia atau membina sistem baharu dari awal, sebaliknya elemen NLHI boleh disesuaikan dengan sistem kesihatan dan keadaan pasaran setiap negara.
Sebagai contoh, katanya, LungShield boleh diperkenalkan melalui syarikat insurans yang sudah beroperasi di beberapa negara Asean.
Katanya, Malaysia juga telah merundingkan harga dengan penyedia teknologi bagi pihak rantau itu, bukan hanya untuk pasaran tempatan.
Beliau berkata, negara lain juga boleh menggunakan kadar yang dirunding Malaysia, sambil menyifatkannya sebagai contoh 'semangat kejiranan' di rantau ini.
98a904c6a90ff4ac: COPENHAGEN: The international future of Portugal superstar Cristiano Ronaldo hung in the balance after the 41-year-old walked out on the squad after learning that he would not start the game against Denmark on Thursday.

Ronaldo announced late on Wednesday that he had left the team, shortly after a press conference in which coach Jorge Jesus confirmed the five-time Ballon d'Or winner would be left out of his starting line-up for a second consecutive Nations League game.
In his absence, Portugal turned on the style to beat Denmark 4-2.
The former Real Madrid forward had been due to train with his teammates at the Parken Stadium on the eve of the game, but walked out following the announcement by Jesus.

"Following the national team coach's press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team's training camp," Ronaldo wrote on Instagram.
He had already spent the entirety of Sunday's 2-1 Nations League win in Norway on the bench, having captained the side in the 1-0 home victory over Wales last Thursday.
Ronaldo appeared to indicate that the reasons behind Jesus's decision ran deeper, and hinted at a departure from the national team he has graced for more than two decades.
"In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated," Ronaldo said.
"Now is time to wish good luck to Portugal and to all my team-mates, without exception."

Spanish sports daily Marca said that Jesus and Portuguese federation president Pedro Proenca followed Ronaldo to Copenhagen airport in an attempt to persuade him to stay with the squad, before the player boarded his private jet.

Jesus insisted earlier on Wednesday that there was no rift between him and Ronaldo, although the 72-year-old, who was appointed in July, acknowledged that his captain was disappointed to remain on the bench against Norway.
The news sparked a wave of memes on social media and a furious backlash from Ronaldo's sister, Elma Aveiro.
"They don't deserve to have the best of anything," she said about the Portuguese people on Instagram.
"We are envious, scornful, and ignorant, and we deserve to return to the mediocrity that defined us in the pre-CR7 era of football," she added, using his nickname.
- 'PLAYERS WITH STATUS' -
The game in Oslo was the first time since November 2024 that Ronaldo had not featured for Portugal while not being either injured or suspended.
"There was no incident whatsoever," Jesus, who coached Ronaldo at Saudi club Al-Nassr for a year, insisted after that match.
"Any player – and I was a player myself... when you spend 20 or 30 minutes warming up and then don't get on... no one is happy about that," Jesus added on Wednesday.
The Portuguese coach also said that he had told Ronaldo before the match that he might bring him on as a substitute.
"Afterwards, as coach, I decided not to bring him on. It's nothing to make a fuss about," Jesus insisted.
After the win on Thursday, Jesus's press conference was dominated by talk of Ronaldo.
"This Portugal team scored four goals and put in a performance which, in my opinion, was of a very high standard," he said.
"Of course, this is more important than anything else that has happened.
"I still think exactly the same way: there are players with status. That much is crystal clear," he added.
"But I'll say it again: the rules are the same for everyone."
There were reports that Portuguese Prime Minister Luis Montenegro had even discussed the issue of Ronaldo's involvement with the coach on Wednesday.
Jesus said earlier in the day that against Denmark he again intended to start AC Milan striker Goncalo Ramos, who scored the winner in Norway.
Regarding Ronaldo, he said: "If I need him, he'll come on. If I don't need him, he won't."
Ronaldo recently announced that this would "probably (be) my last year in football."
He is Portugal's leading goalscorer and most capped player, with 146 goals in 234 appearances.
The former Sporting, Manchester United, Real and Juventus striker made his international debut aged 18 in 2003 and played in the Euro 2004 final when Portugal lost to hosts Greece.
He reached the World Cup semi-finals in 2006 and captained his country to glory at Euro 2016.
Ronaldo and Portugal were eliminated by eventual winners Spain in the last 16 of this year's World Cup.--AFP

cf231b6d067810c4: MEDINA: The Saudi-led coalition fighting Yemen's Houthis said on Thursday the group had attacked a power distribution station in Medina, one of Islam's holiest sites, this week, putting one transformer out of service but without affecting the electricity network.
Hours after the coalition's accusation, the Houthis reported Saudi strikes on the Yemeni capital of Sanaa and other parts of Yemen, with no immediate Saudi confirmation of the reports.
The recent escalation is the most serious fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Iran-aligned Houthis since a UN-brokered truce largely halted cross-border attacks in 2022.

Hostilities resumed this year after the Houthis declared a naval blockade on Saudi Arabia in July and began attacking Saudi territory and shipping, while Houthi forces also made major territorial gains along Yemen's Red Sea coast.
Saudi Arabia has responded with airstrikes in Yemen and backed government forces fighting to repel the Houthis.

The Saudi-led coalition said an investigation and examination of drone wreckage confirmed Houthi involvement in planning and carrying out Tuesday's attack on the Medina power station. It said the station supplies electricity to the Prophet's Mosque, one of Islam's holiest sites.

A Houthi military source, quoted by the Houthi-run Saba news agency, denied the accusation, calling it a "lie" and saying it was intended to cover up what he described as Saudi Arabia's failure to substantiate its earlier accusation that the Houthis targeted the Muslim holy city of Mecca.

Saudi Arabia said two weeks ago it had intercepted and destroyed a Houthi drone south of Mecca before it entered restricted airspace over the city. The coalition described that incident as the second Houthi attempt to target Mecca since 2017, while the Houthis denied targeting Mecca or any other Islamic holy site.

The coalition said the Medina attack was part of what it described as repeated Houthi attempts to target the Two Holy Mosques and "provoke" Muslims worldwide. It said it would continue taking measures to protect the holy sites and pilgrims.

The Houthis said later in the day that Saudi Arabia had carried out strikes on Sanaa and the provinces of Saada, Taiz and Amran, according to their news agency. While there was no Saudi confirmation, the Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces said on X they had carried out more than two dozen airstrikes against Houthi positions in Taiz, targeting missile storage, command centres and other military sites.
The reported strike on Sanaa would be the first since July, when Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces struck the runway at Sanaa airport to prevent an Iranian plane from landing.
f36378581a7c2fa6: KUALA LUMPUR: General practitioners (GPs) are seeing more patients with respiratory complaints, but private hospitals say they are coping with the haze for now.
With the haze expected to linger for two more weeks, doctors are concerned about the effects of prolonged exposure to polluted air, particularly among vulnerable individuals.
Symptoms include coughing, throat irritation, blocked or runny nose, eye irritation, wheezing and asthma exacerbations.
Federation of Private Medical Practitioners' Associations president Dr G. Shanmuganathan said GPs were seeing more patients with symptoms associated with poor air quality.

"If unhealthy air quality persists for another month, GP clinics should anticipate increasing consultations for cough, throat and eye irritation, wheezing, asthma exacerbations and worsening of existing conditions.
"The concern is not simply one day of exposure. It is repeated exposure over several weeks, particularly among vulnerable individuals," he told the New Straits Times.
Dr Shanmuganathan said, however, it was important to distinguish these symptoms from upper respiratory tract infections (URTI).
He said the haze did not cause viral URTI, but symptoms could overlap and pollution could aggravate existing respiratory illnesses.

"From the primary-care perspective, if this episode is expected to persist until this month, it would also be useful for the Health Ministry to monitor respiratory attendances in both public and private primary care.
"This would give us an objective picture of the health burden of prolonged haze exposure, rather than having to rely on anecdotal reports from individual clinics."
Meanwhile, Association of Private Hospitals Malaysia president Datuk Dr Kuljit Singh said private hospitals were not seeing any significant increase in admissions linked to the haze.
He said private hospitals were managing respiratory and haze-related cases well and had the capacity to respond should patient numbers increase.
He said there was no pressure on bed occupancy or respiratory wards at present.
Dr Kuljit said this was supported by close collaboration between private hospitals, public hospitals and the Health Ministry, allowing for appropriate referrals and coordinated care when required.
"We typically see fluctuations in influenza cases several times throughout the year, and this trend is observed across both private and public hospitals.
"While haze does not directly cause influenza, exposure to poor air quality can aggravate existing respiratory conditions and symptoms, including those associated with influenza and bronchitis."

Dr Kuljit said the association continued to work closely with the ministry to ensure patients received appropriate care and that the healthcare system remained prepared should respiratory and haze-related cases increase further.

fcd2cd74c2ccc4ab: NEW YORK: A judge on Thursday denied an acquittal request by an American mother accused of murdering her three children, a court filing showed, weeks after a jury failed to reach a verdict in the high-profile case.

During the trial, 36-year-old Lindsay Clancy did not deny strangling Cora, age five, Dawson, three, and Callan, eight months. But she claimed she was suffering from postpartum psychosis and sought to be excused from criminal responsibility.
Judge William Sullivan, of the Plymouth court near Boston, ruled there was sufficient evidence to convince a juror of Clancy's guilt.
The judge has yet to decide whether she will face a retrial.
In September a jury of nine women and three men was unable to reach a unanimous decision, as required in criminal proceedings in the United States, leading to a mistrial.
Kevin Reddington, who is defending Clancy, had asked the judge to enter a not-guilty verdict, essentially dismissing the case after a weeks-long, televised trial that captivated Americans.

"Where is the evidence she did this?" said Reddington previously. He also cast doubt on Clancy's own admissions that she killed her children, in what would be a major shift from her mental health defense.
Prosecutor Jennifer Sprague disputed the claim of insufficient evidence as a "laughable argument."
Eleven jurors were in favour of finding Clancy not guilty by reason of insanity, but they were opposed by a single holdout who has spoken publicly about being sure of her guilt.
The prosecution opposed the disclosures, saying they would have a "chilling effect" on the lone juror.
Clancy's trial, which featured more than 80 witnesses and days of distressing testimony, sparked debate in the United States over maternal mental health.
President Donald Trump has called the case a "horrible tragedy" and said he assumed there would be another trial.
Clancy, who is being held at a psychiatric institution, pleaded not guilty by reason of insanity and said she heard a voice ordering her to kill her children.
Her lawyers said this was caused by postpartum psychosis, a condition that medical experts say affects about one to two women in every 1,000 births.
Prosecutors rejected that argument, saying Clancy had carefully planned the murders and was able to understand the consequences of her actions.

After the killings at the family home in Duxbury, Massachusetts in January 2023, Clancy cut her neck and wrists and jumped from a second-story window in an apparent suicide attempt that has left her paralysed from the waist down and confined to a wheelchair.--AFP
17914c3097a9e275: KUALA LUMPUR, Oct 2 — The government has expanded electricity bill protection to domestic users consuming up to 800 kilowatt-hours (kWh) a month, up from the previous 600kWh limit.

The temporary protection, which applies to electricity consumption from September 1 to December 31, exempts eligible households from the Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA), retail charge and eight per cent Sales and Service Tax (SST).
But what does 800kWh actually mean for an ordinary household?
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said the government expanded electricity bill protection to households using up to 800kWh a month. — Bernama pic
What is 800kWh?
A kilowatt-hour, or kWh, is a unit used to measure how much electricity you use.
A household using 800kWh over a 30-day month averages about 26.7kWh a day.

According to Tenaga Nasional Berhad (TNB), household electricity consumption depends on factors including the power rating and efficiency of appliances, how many hours they are used, the number of appliances and household usage patterns.
Why was the threshold increased?

Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said recent haze and hotter weather had caused some households to use more electricity, pushing their consumption above the previous 600kWh threshold and resulting in higher bills.
The protection was therefore expanded to 800kWh.
This does not mean electricity tariffs have been permanently reduced.
Instead, households consuming 800kWh or less receive temporary exemptions from the AFA, retail charge and SST until the end of December.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Haze and hotter weather have contributed to higher electricity use among some households. — Picture by the Sayuti Zainudin
How much electricity does an appliance use?
If you are not sure how much is your power consumption, TNB has a formula to estimate an appliance’s monthly electricity consumption:
Electricity consumption (kWh) = Power rating (watts) × hours of operation × 30 days ÷ 1,000.
For example, a 100W appliance used for 10 hours a day would consume:
100W × 10 hours × 30 ÷ 1,000 = 30kWh a month.
A 500W appliance used for two hours a day would also consume:
500W × 2 hours × 30 ÷ 1,000 = 30kWh a month.
Almost everything plugged into your home contributes to the total, including lights, fans, televisions, laptops, washing machines, rice cookers, kettles, water heaters and air-conditioners.
Here are some examples of appliances’ monthly electricity use:
What happens if your household uses 800kWh, less or more?
Under the expanded protection, households using 800kWh or less a month are exempted from the Automatic Fuel Adjustment (AFA), RM10 retail charge and SST.
How much a household saves depends on how much electricity it uses and the AFA rate for that billing period.
The maximum saving is estimated at about RM47 a month, although the amount will differ between households.
This is because the AFA rate can change based on factors such as fuel costs and foreign exchange movements.
Households using more than 800kWh a month will not receive these exemptions.
Consumers should therefore check the kWh figure on their electricity bill, rather than looking only at the total amount payable.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Air-conditioners are among the household appliances that can contribute significantly to monthly electricity consumption. — Unsplash pic
What does 800kWh look like in everyday use?
There is no typical “800kWh household” because electricity use differs depending on the size of the home, number of occupants, appliances and how often they are used.
Think of 800kWh as the total electricity used by everything in your home over one month.
This includes air-conditioners, refrigerators, water heaters, cooking appliances, washing machines, lights, fans, televisions and computers.
For example, an appliance that uses 30kWh a month makes up about 3.75 per cent of the 800kWh threshold.
Several appliances that use relatively small amounts of electricity can therefore add up quickly over a month.
The 800kWh threshold also does not mean households receive 800kWh of free electricity.
It simply determines whether a household qualifies for the temporary exemptions from the specified charges.
ea9a1b8973a00b4b: STOCKHOLM, Oct 2 — Donald Trump’s intense campaigning last year for the Nobel Peace Prize has left the awarding committee treading carefully for this year’s pick, experts said ahead of next week’s prize announcement.
The US president’s outspoken calls to be given the accolade put the five-member committee under unprecedented pressure last year.

The situation grew even more delicate when the laureate, Venezuelan opposition leader Maria Corina Machado, later gave Trump her Nobel gold medal, judging he deserved it after the capture of President Nicolas Maduro.
The Nobel jury knows it is being closely watched by the US president again this year.
“There’s always a lot of lobbying, and ultimately perhaps also attempts to exert pressure on the committee,” the secretary of the Nobel committee, Kristian Berg Harpviken, told AFP in an interview.
“So in one sense we’re very used to that.”
Children, journalists, justice
According to several experts, the Trump saga could lead the committee to choose a laureate who enjoys broad consensus when the name is revealed on October 9.
“After last year’s prize, maybe they’re seeking a less controversial situation this year,” the acting director of the Peace Research Institute of Oslo, Haakon Gjerlow, told AFP.

His favourite pick would be a joint prize to Save the Children and Mykola Kuleba, a Ukrainian children’s rights activist campaigning for the return of Ukrainian children illegally taken to Russia from occupied territories.
This option would have the added benefit of pleasing Trump’s wife Melania, who wrote a letter to Russian President Vladimir Putin in 2025 pleading for the release of Ukrainian children.

Among Gjerlow’s other favourites were Sudan’s Emergency Response Rooms (ERR), a vast network of volunteers risking their lives to help people facing the double threat of war and hunger; the Committee to Protect Journalists (CPJ) after the deadliest year on record for the profession in 2025; and even the International Space Station.

If the committee was prepared to go head-to-head with Trump, other choices could be the UN special rapporteur on the occupied Palestinian territories Francesca Albanese, the International Criminal Court or Pope Leo XIV.
Argentine for literature?
The other closely-watched Nobel is that for literature, to be announced on October 8.
Speculation in Sweden’s literary circles is already in full swing, fuelled by the fact that the list of nominees and the jury’s deliberations are kept secret for 50 years.

After honouring Hungarian author Laszlo Krasznahorkai last year, the Swedish Academy that selects the literature laureate could this time go for a woman writer, possibly from Latin America, according to some literary critics surveyed by AFP.

“In recent years, there has been a lot of talk about the ‘Latin American literary miracle’, this new generation that came after the male authors devoted to magical realism, like Gabriel Garcia Marquez,” said Lina Kalmteg, literary critic at Swedish public radio SR.
“In this new wave, it’s women who are taking the lead, with writing often tinged with feminism, but also often quite dark and violent, punctuated by surreal touches,” she noted.
Argentine author Samanta Schweblin, 48, would be an interesting and surprising choice in this category, she said.
“But she is surely still too young,” she added.
Literature laureates are honoured for their body of work, not a single publication.
Others are putting their money on Antiguan-American author Jamaica Kincaid, whose work deals with exile, identity and the traumas inherited from colonialism, or on Chinese writer Can Xue.
Some “usual suspects” mentioned regularly in Nobel buzz include Australia’s Gerald Murnane, his compatriot Alexis Wright, American author Thomas Pynchon and Mexican writer Cristina Rivera Garza.

The Academy has long been criticised for its focus on male, Western authors. It was rocked by a MeToo scandal in 2018 that left it in tatters, and more than half of its members have since been replaced.
Since then, nearly every other laureate has been a woman.
The Nobel season opens Monday with the medicine prize, which experts say could go to research into the GLP-1 appetite-regulating hormone behind weight-loss drugs like Ozempic.
The physics prize will be announced on Tuesday and chemistry on Wednesday, with the economics prize wrapping up the awards week on October 13.
The Nobel Prize consists of a diploma, a gold medal and a cheque for around US$1.2 million, to be shared if there is more than one laureate in each discipline. — AFP
120a09b0939cd4f4: SEPANG, Oct 2 — After almost a decade in the wilderness, Formula 1 (F1) roars back into Malaysia this weekend but not quite in the way anyone expected.

Instead of the familiar Malaysian Grand Prix (GP), Sepang International Circuit (SIC) will host the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain Grand Prix in Malaysia 2026 from October 2 to 4, turning the iconic Malaysian circuit into the temporary home of Bahrain’s biggest motorsport event.

This came after Formula 1 confirmed Malaysia as host of the upcoming Gulf Air Bahrain GP, following an agreement between Formula 1, the International Automobile Federation (FIA) and governments of Malaysia and Bahrain, in July.
The agreement keeps the Bahrain GP on the 2026 F1 calendar after the race had been cancelled earlier this season due to geopolitical tensions in West Asia.
As SIC is renowned for producing unpredictable races, dramatic weather and memorable championship moments, the timing could hardly be more intriguing.

Since the Malaysian GP was dropped from the F1 calendar after the 2017 season, the sport has undergone a remarkable transformation, with its global fanbase expanding significantly following the launch of Netflix’s Drive to Survive series in 2019.

The series has introduced F1 to a new generation of fans by offering an inside look at the drivers, teams and rivalries behind the sport, helping to broaden its appeal beyond traditional motorsport audiences.
The renewed excitement is also reflected in ticket sales, with around 95,000 three-day passes already sold for the October 2-4 race weekend as SIC targets the 100,000 mark.
Tickets for the Formula 1 Gulf Air Bahrain GP in Malaysia 2026 are sold as three-day passes only with no single-day tickets available for purchase.

Should sales reach 100,000, it would mark a significant turnout for SIC, with the circuit’s highest attendance for an F1 event was recorded during the 2008 Malaysian GP, which attracted 126,690 spectators over the three-day weekend.
Meanwhile, SIC itself could have a major say in how the race unfolds.

Sepang’s layout, featuring long straights and a fast-flowing middle section, will put the cars and drivers through a demanding test, with tyre degradation and the ever-present threat of tropical rain adding further complexity.
The 5.543-kilometre long circuit also hosted one of F1’s most memorable wet-weather races in 2009, when torrential monsoon rain forced officials to red-flag the Malaysian GP after 31 laps.
The Malaysian Meteorological Department has forecast the possibility of rain during Sunday’s race, raising the prospect of another Sepang thriller.
Adding to the challenge is the current haze situation, which could further test the drivers and teams over the race weekend.

Interestingly, only 10 drivers on the current grid have previously raced at the circuit, meaning the experienced and former Malaysian GP champions Aston Martin’s Fernando Alonso, Lewis Hamilton of Ferrari and Red Bull Racing’s Max Verstappen could hold valuable knowledge of the demanding layout.
Alonso stands out with three victories at the circuit, taking the chequered flag for Renault in 2005, McLaren in 2007 and Ferrari in 2012.
Hamilton also tasted success here in 2014 when he represented Mercedes, before Verstappen emerged victorious in the final Malaysian GP in 2017.
Among the new generation of drivers that will make a debut in SIC is the current leader for drivers’ standings with 302 points, Kimi Antonelli of Mercedes.
The 20-year-old Italian will be looking to return to the podium at SIC following a difficult weekend in Azerbaijan GP, where a qualifying crash saw the Italian salvage fifth place in the race.
His teammate, George Russell, meanwhile, arrives in Sepang on a high after claiming his third victory of the season in Azerbaijan GP, cutting Antonelli’s lead to 66 points.
Verstappen, however, cannot be discounted, with former Minardi driver and Malaysian F1 icon Alex Yoong billing the four-time world champion as a dark horse for victory at Sepang.

Reigning world champion Lando Norris, meanwhile, will be looking to bounce back after retiring from the Azerbaijan GP last weekend, with the McLaren driver also facing his first competitive outing at Sepang.

Beyond the high-speed drama on track, Bahrain International Circuit (BIC) chief executive Sheikh Salman Isa Al Khalifa recently said fans can immerse themselves in Bahrain’s culture, traditions and cuisine as the Kingdom showcases its Grand Prix experience in Malaysia.
Nine years on, the wait is finally over.
The engines are ready, the fans are coming and Sepang is ready to roar again. — Bernama
4ed7a5285eaa8665: KOTA TINGGI, Oct 2 — With a family recipe that goes back 19 years, the Jalan Mawai apam balik here continues to draw customers from across the district.
Despite the rising cost of its ingredients, its original flavour is sold for as little as RM4 a piece.
Nelta Efrida Zulfadhli, 37, said all ingredients are prepared daily.
The flour batter is freshly made at the premises, and the corn is prepared in-house instead of from the can.

“We have raised prices previously, but we are mindful of our customers. Given our high sales volume, we have managed to maintain a profit margin and have no plans to raise prices for the time being,” she told Bernama recently.
Her husband, Mohd Shahrizal Supri, 41, represents the second generation to run the family business, which he built using his own capital.
His wife, Nelta Efrida, now a mother of three, joined the business in 2009 after they were engaged.

“Customers are not only from the surrounding areas. Some come from as far as Skudai, Kulai, Simpang Renggam and Mersing just to buy our apam balik,” said Nelta Efrida, who has three full-time and two part-time workers.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Apam Balik Jalan Mawai offers a twist with its plump ‘apam’, which has also become a customer favourite. — Bernama pic
The business started with a daily five kilogrammes (kg) of flour in 2007.
This reached 50 to 55kg daily during the holiday season.
Nelta Efrida said the rise in demand added between RM2,000 and RM2,500 to daily sales on regular days and about RM4,500 during the holiday season.
She said daily sales reached as high as RM6,000 when her apam balik went viral.
The original is the best-seller, followed by Nutella and Japanese-style apam balik with red bean paste.
Other flavours offered include pistachio, matcha, peanut butter and Lotus Biscoff.
She previously supplied her products at events such as public tea receptions in Mersing and Kota Tinggi and at various Hari Raya gatherings in Johor Bahru.
<!--article_body_images.blade.php-->
Nelta Efrida Zulfadhli prepares an ‘apam balik’ order at the Apam Balik Jalan Mawai shop. — Bernama pic
A key challenge of the business is a shortage of workers, particularly when trying to meet local demand during weddings.

“Many have contacted us for orders, but having an additional worker is insufficient. If we take (workers) from another branch, that shop will have to close,” she said, adding that they have another branch in Kota Tinggi town.
Her current focus is to expand her target market via social media platforms such as TikTok instead of opening more branches, to ensure product consistency, she said.
“It is better to focus on one location and reach more people, making sure they know about our shop and products,” she said.
She plans to raise staff count and accept wedding orders next year.
Operations usually begin at around 9.30am, with the last order at 4pm.
However, she has closed her premises as early as 2pm when they sold out. — Bernama
9bde44cbe07aa889: Man always fears death, but the sage welcomes it as a teacher.
On Monday, Dr Hasmah Ali passed away. I will not write about her life, for I hardly knew her beyond the fact that she was the wife of one of my two favourite sons of Malaysia, Dr Mahathir Mohamad.
The other is Anwar Ibrahim, our current prime minister.

On that solemn day, a photograph circulated of Anwar briefly speaking to Mahathir at the mosque before the funeral prayers for Hasmah. That single image brought back three decades of memories, both painful and miraculous.

Mahathir and Anwar are without doubt two men who have shaped a big part of my adult life. They have been the front-page narrators of our nation for more than 40 years, perhaps even 50. No one else comes close.

As a progressive Malay, I once looked to Mahathir for his radical views that defied tradition. He believed passionately in learning, reading and working hard with professionalism and ethics—values Umno today seems to have forgotten.

As an Islamic reformist, I looked to Anwar for the ideals of the Prophet Muhammad that I found in my readings of the hadiths. Between them, I absorbed much of the thought, character and action that has shaped me as a Malay, a Muslim, and a Malaysian.

When Mahathir first rose to power, he was not the favourite among Malays. His ideas were too radical, too disruptive of tradition. He wanted Malays to be as industrious as the Japanese, disciplined and forward-looking. I am similarly disliked by many Malays for calling a spade a spade, and insisting that they equip themselves with intellect and knowledge of our history, culture and religions.

Anwar, meanwhile, believed in an Islam that could move Malays away from race-based majoritarianism and place them on the global platform of progressive Islam. Many Malays dislike him for this, branding him a liberal. PAS went further, calling him a remnant of colonialist kafirs. I, too, have been similarly labelled.

The saddest day for me came when Anwar was imprisoned for sodomy. My hatred towards Mahathir ran deep then. But in 2018, a miracle unfolded. Mahathir walked calmly into the courthouse, shook Anwar’s hand, and said: “Let us work together to get rid of Najib.” Just like that.

I had prayed for Anwar’s protection through his imprisonments and God answered in a way I did not expect—by bringing the old man back to shake his hand. I saw that as divine intervention. I supported their reconciliation, though Mahathir never expressed remorse or apologised for what happened. I told myself time would change him but I was wrong.

But I learned a lesson about realpolitik. To win, you need friends and coalitions. After victory, you may even have to defeat your partners. Mahathir understood this well. Anwar, perhaps, has not, with Umno betraying him in last two state elections.

After 2020, the two were at war again. Mahathir no longer had the clout of a strong party, but his charisma remained. Even in a wheelchair, his words could rock the nation. He did not need to shout like Dr Akmal Saleh or bully like Jamal Yunos. He simply spoke, or wrote, and the nation listened.
In 2022, Mahathir saw his number one enemy—and perhaps his only true “friend”—become prime minister. Another miracle.

Over the four years since then, Anwar has tried to right Barisan Nasional’s wrong and help carry its baggage. Mahathir has also been in attendance, always trying to derail him. He suggestion of the “big tent” for Malays is one that brought Umno into its new marriage with PAS. The old man still had his sting.

And so the rivalry has continued. Until God decided to make one more play. At Hasmah’s funeral, these two great sons of Malaysia shook hands once more. I never thought I would see such an image after the recent Merdeka Day slight.
Yet I respect Mahathir for what he taught me: to be a Malay who loves knowledge, who thinks outside the boxes of religion, politics and work. In fact, Mahathir doesn’t see a box. I share that view.
The day Hasmah left us was solemn and sad, but also reminded us of mortality and purpose. It was a day of coming together after coming apart yet again.
Our lives are too short for hatred and division. Death is the greatest teacher of why we must always come back together.
The views expressed are those of the writer and do not necessarily reflect those of FMT.
cfe2532dd45a52b2: KUALA LUMPUR: When Yeow Teck Chai picks up a paintbrush, he hopes the finished work will find a home. He also hopes it will help someone he may never meet.

The former deputy director-general of the Malaysian Investment Development Authority (Mida) has spent years using his love of painting to raise funds for charity. This month, he will do so again at “Art4Good: Painting from the Heart”.

Running from Oct 14-18 at Bangsar Shopping Centre and supported by FMT, the exhibition will raise funds for two non-profit organisations: Free Food Society (FFS) and the Society for the Severely Mentally Handicapped (SSMH).
Although these organisations help people in different ways, both share the common goal of improving the lives of vulnerable members of society by creating more opportunities for them.
Based in Desa Rejang, Setapak, FFS helps 85 underprivileged families put food on the table and runs tuition classes for their children, using education to help break the cycle of poverty.
At SSMH’s training centre in Petaling Jaya, children with severe disabilities receive rehabilitative therapy tailored to their needs, helping them learn everyday skills to become more independent.

More than 120 paintings will be on display and for sale at the exhibition. Yeow, the principal artist, has contributed almost 100 of them, drawing on a passion for art that has stayed with him since childhood.
Since his first charity exhibition in 2018, sales of more than 400 of his paintings have supported charitable causes. This will be his fourth charity exhibition.

Yeow will be joined by fellow artists Oon Soon Keat, Yoon Chooi Wan and Tan Ken Ming, who has Asperger’s syndrome. Also taking part is eight-year-old Winsen Loke, who has global developmental delay and attends rehabilitative therapy at SSMH.

The exhibition will be officially launched on Oct 14 by former international trade and industry minister Rafidah Aziz. She, too, has contributed eight paintings, which will be sold through a silent auction.
Whether you pause to admire the artworks or find a painting to take home, behind every piece is an artist hoping to bring a little beauty into your day, and a little help to someone who needs it.

9e2805185a206a7b: Apabila istilah 'feminisme' disebut di Malaysia, perdebatan sering menjadi tegang sebelum ia sempat bermula. Sebahagian masyarakat melihatnya sebagai perjuangan menuntut hak yang adil, sebahagian lagi curiga ia membawa gagasan luar yang boleh bertentangan dengan nilai keluarga kita.

Hakikatnya, kita tidak perlu membuang masa bertekak sama ada mahu menerima atau menolak istilah ini seratus peratus. Soal yang lebih mendesak ialah nasib hidup wanita, tanggungjawab mengurus rumah tangga, dan soal mencari rezeki di Malaysia hari ini.

Keadaan ini dapat dilihat melalui angka. Global Gender Gap Report 2026 meletakkan Malaysia di tangga ke-104 daripada 145 ekonomi dalam mengukur jurang antara lelaki dan wanita. Cermin sebenar masyarakat kita pula boleh dilihat pada penyertaan wanita dalam tenaga buruh.

Angka rasmi setakat pertengahan 2026 menunjukkan kadar penyertaan tenaga buruh wanita ialah 57.3%, berbanding lelaki 82.9%. Mengapa jurang ini masih besar sedangkan ramai wanita kita berpelajaran tinggi? Antara perkara perlu diberi perhatian ialah tanggungjawab rumah tangga dan keluarga yang terus mempengaruhi penyertaan seseorang dalam pasaran pekerjaan.

Saban hari, rakyat Malaysia menghabiskan purata lebih lima jam untuk kerja rumah dan menjaga ahli keluarga tanpa bayaran. Namun, wanita menanggung bahagian lebih besar dengan purata enam jam tujuh minit sehari, berbanding lelaki empat jam 20 minit.

Apabila anak sakit, sekolah ditutup, atau ibu bapa semakin uzur, siapa yang biasanya perlu mengorbankan masa kerja? Angka ini bukan untuk menyalahkan sesiapa, tetapi membuka mata bahawa tempat kerja dan masyarakat kita masih perlu melakukan lebih banyak usaha untuk membantu pasangan suami isteri membahagikan tanggungjawab dengan lebih seimbang.

Sebab itulah perbincangan berhubung hak lelaki dan wanita di Malaysia tidak boleh dicedok bulat-bulat dari Barat. Kehidupan wanita profesional di ibu kota jauh bezanya daripada ibu tunggal di kampung. Perjalanan hidup mereka dibentuk oleh pendapatan, agama, latar sosial, dan adat resam.

Di negara kita, agama dan keluarga bukan sekadar urusan peribadi, tetapi tiang seri masyarakat. Sebarang usaha untuk membela nasib wanita mesti berakar pada nilai keadilan, amanah, dan kebaikan bersama yang dekat dengan kehidupan masyarakat kita, bukan sekadar meminjam laungan dari luar.

Layanan yang adil juga tidak bermakna wujudnya perang antara lelaki dan wanita. Lelaki juga seorang bapa, anak, suami, dan rakan sekerja. Galakan agar lelaki sama-sama menjaga anak dan melakukan kerja rumah bukan sekadar meringankan beban isteri, malah membantu membentuk keluarga yang lebih bertanggungjawab. Perbincangan yang sihat tidak mencari musuh; ia mencari jalan keluar.

Pada akhirnya, kita berdepan soal peluang, pekerjaan, tanggungjawab keluarga, dan layanan yang saksama setiap hari. Kita boleh meneliti pandangan dari luar untuk memahami keadaan, namun jalan penyelesaian mesti sesuai dengan acuan tempatan.
Yang penting bukan memenangkan istilah 'feminisme', tetapi keberanian kita membina masyarakat dan sistem adil buat lelaki dan wanita.
Penulis ialah calon PhD bidang pengajian kepimpinan yang mengkaji kepimpinan responsif, adil dan seimbang antara lelaki dan wanita.
Artikel ini adalah pandangan penulis dan tidak semestinya mewakili FMT.
858268099f5bcdb3: DUBLIN: The Nations League football match between Ireland and Austria in Dublin on Thursday was twice briefly interrupted by demonstrations in support of the Palestine.
In the 19th minute, spectators threw tennis balls covered in Palestinian flag stickers onto the field.
The players left the pitch for a few minutes before the match resumed.
In the 35th minute, a man ran onto the pitch waving a Palestinian flag, briefly interrupting the match again.
The game ended in a 2–2 draw.
The incidents follow the controversy surrounding Sunday's Nations League match between Ireland and Israel.
After lengthy discussions about a boycott, in protest against the war in Gaza, the Irish players finally decided to play the match, which took place in Hungary in a virtually empty stadium.
The Irish players, who won 3–0, wore black armbands, and the captains of both teams did not shake hands or exchange pennants before kick-off.
The return leg is scheduled for Sunday, once again on neutral ground in Serbia, as the Irish Football Association deemed organising the match at home too sensitive.
On Thursday evening, around 200 protesters gathered outside the Dublin Arena as part of a campaign called "Stop the Game".
"I strongly object to these two games against Israel going ahead, because basically it is sports-washing a genocide, sports are political.
"And it's happened many, many a time where people have boycotted events," said Joanne Doyle, a 56-year-old primary school teacher.
She was one of around 200 protesting outside the stadium in Dublin.
"Ireland should not be playing ball with genocide. We've already played one game against genocidal Israel and crossed the Palestinian picket line." said Mark Coomey, a 26-year-old engineer.
Ireland, alongside Spain and Norway, recognised a Palestinian state in 2024 and has repeatedly criticised Israel over the Gaza conflict.
48df2717a100b3ff: WASHINGTON: The Pentagon on Thursday announced the award of a US$24.4 billion contract for Raytheon to accelerate production of SM-6 missiles as Washington works to replace the large amount of munitions expended during the Iran war.
The missiles are "critical anti-air and anti-surface warfare munition. This five-year agreement, with two additional option years, will drive faster production," the Pentagon said in a statement.
The deal "provides the defence industry with the long-term predictability needed to expand workforce capacity and secure critical supply chains," the statement added.
President Donald Trump has so far brushed aside questions about the major toll taken on US munition supplies by the war against Iran, which the United States and Israel launched on Feb 28.

But the Defence Department's inspector general said last month that "the munitions expenditure on Operation Epic Fury has resulted in strategic inventory shortfalls and revealed industrial base bottlenecks for munitions resupply," using the official name for the operation against Iran.
And a Sept 15 report by the Congressional Budget Office cited the hit to missile defence supplies that "will leave the United States with a reduced inventory of interceptors for several years."

Teheran continues to exert control over the strategic Strait of Hormuz more than seven months after the initial US and Israeli attacks on the Islamic Republic, while Washington is blockading Iran's ports.

Trump has told aides he expects to resume bombing Iran by late November, the Wall Street Journal reported, which would set the stage for further Iranian strikes and more expenditures of American munitions.--AFP

ca277fc1b630f6f1: MILWAUKEE: The United States on Thursday told its European allies to help lower global diesel prices by releasing strategic reserves "immediately," with EU member states due to discuss the crisis on Friday.
Reports said the Trump administration wants France and Germany in particular to tap their stockpiles of diesel to try to curb prices sent soaring by the US war on Iran.

"Our European partners should accelerate delivery on their existing commitments and make additional supplies immediately available to address ongoing disruptions," US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said in a post on social media.
EU member states will meet with the European Commission Friday to discuss a coordinated response to soaring fuel prices, a Commission spokesman said.
Washington is piling on pressure to get European help with fuel costs, with US President Donald Trump on Wednesday floating the possibility of banning diesel exports.
High energy costs loom as a threat to Trump's Republican party in next month's midterm elections.
"It is in Europe's best interest to work with the United States as we pursue multiple pathways to boost the supply of refined products and lower costs for consumers," a US official told AFP.
At G20 trade talks in Milwaukee, US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer struck a conciliatory tone, saying there was an "eagerness on both sides to work together" on the diesel issue.
And Trump told reporters in Texas on Thursday that he "may" ask European countries to release diesel reserves.
- 'UNEXPECTED' -
Still, EU trade chief Maros Sefcovic told reporters Thursday that any move by the US to ban diesel exports would be "unexpected for Europeans."
He spoke on the sidelines of the two-day G20 trade ministers' gathering in Milwaukee, after meeting with Greer.
Sefcovic told reporters that he did not go into details with Greer on energy exports.
But the transatlantic partners "decided to stay in close touch to avoid any surprises here," he said.
"It would have very dramatic consequences for our economic performance," Sefcovic said of any potential diesel export ban.
France's minister delegate for international trade, Nicolas Forissier, told AFP in Milwaukee: "I can't imagine that there will be a ban."
He stressed the importance of diesel to the United States and European countries, adding both sides will "try to find solutions."
"In France, we'll try to find balanced solutions all over the world," Forissier added. "If not with the Americans, it will be with other countries."
Trump on Wednesday said he was still considering a possible ban on US diesel exports, while adding that he thought it could ultimately cause gasoline prices to rise.
"I'm thinking about it," Trump told reporters in the Oval Office.
Speaking alongside Trump, US Energy Secretary Chris Wright said Wednesday that the world would "hear announcements from our friends in Europe" to push diesel prices down.
Asked about a release from strategic reserves, the French presidency said no such demand had been made when Emmanuel Macron and Trump met on the sidelines of the UN General Assembly last week.

Macron would also soon convene a video meeting of G7 leaders "to make progress on the various levers that can be used to address the rising fuel prices... including coordination on releasing reserves."
Macron announced on Sept 18 a plan for such a meeting. The G7 gathering is expected in mid-October, according to Macron's press office.
Average US diesel prices have surged more than 70 per cent to US$6.39 a gallon since the start of the Iran war, according to AAA motor club data.
Fuel prices have caused living costs to soar, leaving Trump's Republican Party fearing it could lose control of Congress in November's midterm elections.--AFP

ec06adfe8d012e82: SAINT-DENIS: New France coach Zinedine Zidane insisted Thursday he has no regrets about his infamous headbutt on Marco Materazzi in the 2006 World Cup final as he prepares to come up against Italy again in his first home game in charge.

"The images will always be there to remind me of what happened in 2006, because they are always being shown," Zidane smiled when asked about the incident which led to him being sent off in extra time in what was his last ever match as a player.

"Fortunately that is not the only thing I did and there were other nicer things, so I try to think more about the positives," Zidane said at a press conference at the Stade de France, where Les Bleus host the Italians in the Uefa Nations League on Friday.
"I don't have regrets because it was part of my career," he continued, adding that he had not spoken to Materazzi since that night in Berlin, in a final which Italy won on penalties.
"In 2006 I didn't know I was going to become a coach. I thought that was the end so it was really difficult for me.
"I am not proud of what happened. I have said it over and over again, but it is part of my career - you can't only do wonderful things," he said.
Zidane, 54, was appointed France coach in late July, succeeding his former international teammate Didier Deschamps, who stepped down after 14 years in charge following the World Cup in North America.
The former Real Madrid coach's first two matches in charge have come away from home, with Les Bleus winning 1-0 in Turkey and by the same scoreline in Belgium in the Nations League.

Friday's match, in front of what will be a sell-out crowd of close to 80,000 at the national stadium to the north of Paris, will therefore be a homecoming for the coach, who remains an icon in France.
"It is going to be really emotional," said Zidane, whose last appearance at the Stade de France came as a player in a friendly against Mexico in 2006.
France are without captain Kylian Mbappe, who returned to his club Real Madrid after suffering a knee injury while scoring the winning goal in Turkey last week.
Earlier, France forward Ousmane Dembele insisted there was no tension between him and Mbappe after comments made by both players in the media about the Ballon d'Or.
Dembele, of Paris Saint-Germain, won last year's Ballon d'Or and is nominated again this year, while Mbappe is one of the leading contenders to succeed his compatriot.
"There is no issue. We have talked about it. We sit next to each other at the dinner table," Dembele told reporters, dismissing the matter as a "social media squabble".
Mbappe said in an interview last month with France Football magazine that Dembele "was always seen as a talented player, while I was always seen as the chosen one".

A few days later, Dembele replied to those comments, saying: "I have never been the chosen one, but I have worked hard, and last year I was rewarded for a fantastic year with Paris Saint-Germain. This year we will see".

7fb8a4258cf468f5: NEW YORK: General Motors reported a dip in third-quarter auto sales Thursday on plunging electric vehicle transactions, while both Toyota and Hyundai rode greater hybrid demand to sales increases.
GM reported deliveries of 670,974, down 5.5% from the year-ago level, with gains in some gasoline-powered vehicles failing to completely offset lower EV sales.

In the 2025 period, GM and other automakers saw a boom in EV sales as US consumers flocked to dealerships ahead of the expiration of a tax credit on Sept 30, 2025 following a policy change backed by US president Donald Trump.
But the surge in third-quarter 2025 EV sales translated into a more than 90% decline in GM's sales of the electric version of the Chevrolet Equinox SUV in the just-finished quarter.
While the gasoline-version Equinox also saw a modest decline compared with last year, GM pointed to smaller sport utility vehicles as a strong point in the quarter.
Overall sales of "affordable small SUVs" were up 27 % said GM, with the Chevrolet Trax, Chevrolet Trailblazer and Buick Envista all higher.

Although persistent inflation continues to weigh on consumers, shoppers are still going to dealerships and purchasing cars, in some cases trading "down" to lower-cost options if they can't afford their first choice, auto analysts say.
Cox Automotive estimated that overall third-quarter US sales would be 4.1 million units, down 0.7% from the year ago level.
While the disappearance of the EV tax credit, worth up to US$7,500 per vehicle, hurt GM's electric fleet, other automakers saw strong hybrid sales in a period of high gasoline prices.
Toyota notched a 0.6% increase in third-quarter sales to 633,223, propelled by 29.2% growth in "electrified vehicles," a division dominated by hybrids at the Japanese brand.
"Our third-quarter results reinforce a simple truth - customers want choices," said Toyota senior vice president Andrew Gilleland.
"From affordability to electrification, our multi-path strategy continues to meet customers where they are and give them options that fit their lifestyles."

Hyundai also saw an uptick in hybrid sales, which rose 35% during the quarter. Overall sales for the South Korean company, which also holds a large stake in Kia, came in at 483,555 vehicles, up 5.4% from the year-ago level.
33b2c6a172d21655: MUNICH: Jurgen Klopp celebrated his first win as Germany manager on Thursday as his side eased to a 2-0 win against Serbia in the third fixture of their UEFA Nations League campaign.
Liverpool's Florian Wirtz and Bayern Munich's Tom Bischof both found the net as a youthful Germany made short work of a lacklustre Serbia team in Munich.
It was a win that lifted the pressure on the new national team boss, after he began his tenure with a 1-1 draw against the Netherlands and a shock 1-0 defeat to Greece last weekend.
Another loss, or a draw, would have made Klopp the first Germany coach in history not to win any of his first three games in charge.
Instead, victory marked a cautious sense of optimism for the four-time world champions, as they look to return to the international elite under Klopp.
"The mix of football and attitude was top level today. I told the boys that this has to be our benchmark," Klopp told public broadcaster ZDF.
His players sang his praises in return.
"Jurgen is a coach that pulls people along with him. We saw that today and I hope it continues into the future," said Bischof.
Having nominated a bumper squad of 44 players for his first round of games, Klopp fielded an entirely new starting eleven against Serbia, including three debutants.

Bayern Munich goalkeeper Jonas Urbig, Freiburg forward Derry Scherhant and Brentford midfielder Vitaly Janelt all made their national team debuts, while Celtic's Mika Baur became the 1,000th player ever to represent Germany when he came on as a 77th minute substitute.
The young team showed a marked improvement on the turgid performance against Greece last Sunday, albeit against underwhelming opposition.
Aleksandar Pavlovic, Serge Gnabry and Bischof all had chances in the first half hour, while Serbia mustered only one dangerous counter-attack through Filip Kostic.
The hosts finally broke through shortly before half-time thanks to some elegant footwork from Wirtz.
Wirtz danced through a maze of legs in the box and hit the post, before an unmarked Bischof smashed the ball in on the rebound.
- 'Flo, Flo, Flo, Wirtz, Wirtz, Wirtz' -
The game continued in the same vein after the break, as Germany continued to pin Serbia back into their own final third.
Juventus' Nick Woltemade should have doubled the lead on 59 minutes but skied the ball high over the bar from a metre in front of goal.
Wirtz spared his team-mate's blushes a moment later, making space for himself in the box with a brilliant first touch and slotting the ball into the bottom corner.
Klopp reserved special praise for the Liverpool player, who has faced criticism in England for his club form recently.
"The rhythm has to be: easy, easy, easy, Flo, Flo, Flo, Wirtz, Wirtz, Wirtz," said the Germany coach. "A performance like that helps us, but it also helps him.
"If he was out of form, we wouldn't just let him play anyway. But he's in form and he showed that in training and today."
The second goal put the win beyond doubt, prompting a Mexican wave to roll around the Munich arena. -AFP

b78a52b9d0bb6d63: DUBLIN: The Nations League football match between Ireland and Austria in Dublin on Thursday was twice briefly interrupted by demonstrations in support of Palestine.
In the 19th minute, spectators threw tennis balls covered in Palestinian flag stickers onto the field.
The players left the pitch for a few minutes before the match resumed.
In the 35th minute, a man ran onto the pitch waving a Palestinian flag, briefly interrupting the match again.

Ireland's Icelandic coach Heimir Hallgrimsson said afterwards that "you are never happy with this (protests), but understand it and respect it."

After lengthy discussions about a boycott, in protest against the war in Gaza, the Irish players finally decided to play the match, which took place in Hungary in a virtually empty stadium.
The Irish players, who won 3-0, wore black armbands, and the captains of both teams did not shake hands or exchange pennants before kick-off.
The return leg is scheduled for Sunday, once again on neutral ground in Serbia, as the Irish Football Association deemed organising the match at home too sensitive.
On Thursday evening, around 200 protesters gathered outside the Dublin Arena as part of a campaign called "Stop the Game."

"I strongly object to these two games against Israel going ahead, because basically it is sports-washing a genocide, sports are political. And it's happened many, many a time where people have boycotted events," said Joanne Doyle, a 56-year-old primary school teacher.
She was one of around 200 protesting outside the stadium in Dublin.
"Ireland should not be playing ball with genocide. We've already played one game against genocidal Israel and crossed the Palestinian picket line." said Mark Coomey, a 26-year-old engineer.
Ireland, alongside Spain and Norway, recognised a Palestinian state in 2024 and has repeatedly criticised Israel over the Gaza conflict.--AFP
3dc23902780a9776: Venus is shrouded in a veil of mystery. The yellowish “lower haze” at the bottom of its atmosphere was discovered by the Venera and Pioneer Venus probes in the 1970s. These spacecraft were some of the first to successfully send images of the planet back to Earth, but the haze they saw went unexplained for decades. Now the mystery Venus was keeping has been unveiled.

What nobody knew then was that the haze is an accumulation of particles from meteorites. “Shooting stars” that burn up in the atmosphere leave behind cosmic dust particles, and after sulfuric acid interacts with these particles, it leaves behind a haze. Planetary scientist Hiroki Karyu and his research team at Tohoku University in Sendai City, Japan, finally figured out how the haze formed using a microphysical model. This type of model involves microphysics—the micro-scale processes that create clouds and precipitation on Earth and other bodies.

“The continuous influx of cosmic dust is sufficient to sustain this lower haze layer with the particle size distribution observed by the entry probes,” Karyu said in a study published in Nature Astronomy. “These haze particles of cosmic origin act as efficient condensation nuclei, promoting cloud formation in the main cloud deck even far from their initial source.”
ae92ae58848bb7e8: COPENHAGEN: Portugal put the controversy surrounding Cristiano Ronaldo's departure to one side as they edged Denmark 4-2 in the UEFA Nations League on Thursday.
Joao Felix made the win safe late in the second half after the hosts had twice fought back to level.

With the pre-match build-up dominated by five-time Ballon d'Or winner Ronaldo's sudden departure from the team's training camp on Wednesday, coach Jorge Jesus said before kick-off that he just wanted his side "to focus on the match."
His team showed no signs of being distracted by the furore caused by the 41-year-old's walk-out after Jesus announced Ronaldo would not start the match against Denmark.
"A victory of the highest quality; this Portugal team scored four goals and put in a performance which, in my opinion, was of a very high standard," Jesus told his post-match press conference.
"I still think exactly the same way: there are players with status. That much is crystal clear.
"But I'll say it again: the rules are the same for everyone. That's a method I've followed throughout my coaching career and I'll continue to follow."
Ronaldo, Portugal's record goalscorer, had already spent all of Sunday's 2-1 Nations League win in Norway on the bench, having captained the side in the 1-0 home victory over Wales last Thursday.

"Following the national team coach's press conference, and after having a conversation with the Portuguese Football Federation president, I decided to leave the national team's training camp," Ronaldo wrote on Instagram on Wednesday.
"In due course, I will tell the truth to all the Portuguese people about my reasons for leaving the national team, to which I have always been dedicated."
On the pitch, Joao Cancelo opened the scoring for Portugal inside 13 minutes, before Mikkel Damsgaard curled in a leveller 10 minutes later.
Goncalo Ramos repaid Jesus's faith in starting him again up front by restoring his country's lead two minutes later with a cute near-post finish.
Rasmus Hojlund equalised for Denmark early in the second period, but Paris Saint-Germain lynchpin Vitinha nodded the visitors back in front in the 57th minute.
Substitute Felix then tucked home at the end of a swift counter-attack with three minutes remaining to give new boss Jesus a third win from his first three matches.

"This is more important than anything else that has happened," Jesus added, before looking ahead to a home game against Norway on Sunday. "So that is what I want to focus on: the match, the next match."--AFP

KOTA KINABALU: The Eastern Sabah Security Command (Esscom) will protect undocumented and stateless communities from exploitation amid cross-border threats.

Its commander, Datuk Victor Sanjos, said the lack of valid identification, limited access to formal employment, socioeconomic factors and the location of some communities could create conditions that might be exploited by irresponsible parties.
"Women and children are among those requiring protection," he told the New Straits Times.
Victor said Esscom also took into account threats including cross-border crime, syndicate activities and exploitation.
Measures would include verifying individuals' identities to distinguish between victims of exploitation, individuals requiring protection and suspects of criminal offences, he said.
"Any information relating to human trafficking, forced labour, smuggling or syndicate activities will be assessed and, if necessary, coordinated with the appropriate agencies for further action.
"Matters involving documentation, welfare and social protection fall under the jurisdiction of several government agencies. This requires scrutiny and inter-agency cooperation."
On Wednesday, the NST reported the exploitation of undocumented Bajau Laut youths for labour in Semporna.

Universiti Malaysia Sabah's Social Sciences and Humanities Faculty lecturer Associate Professor Wan Shawaluddin Wan Hassan said increased maritime security measures, conservation restrictions and declining marine resources had reduced the areas where some members of the community could fish and move.
Following the 2013 Lahad Datu intrusion, increased security measures by Malaysia, the Philippines and Indonesia have further restricted such areas.
Meanwhile, Victor said a community-based approach was also important in protecting vulnerable groups, particularly in island and coastal areas.
He said local communities could help authorities identify suspicious activities.
"They can be the eyes and ears, as well as Esscom's mobile intelligence network, particularly in areas that are difficult for authorities to reach."
205e262e061d63e0: A four-person crew rocketed into orbit Thursday from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, heading for a six-month expedition on the International Space Station.

The launch was delayed from mid-September to replace a balky valve in the Dragon spacecraft's propulsion system, a task that involved cutting into a propellant line inside the ship to swap out a faulty component.

130da346abc61c9f: NEW YORK: Wall Street stocks edged higher Thursday, shrugging off weakness in European equities and the latest jump in oil prices.

Wall Street stocks veered in and out of negative territory during the day, but finished higher. The broad-based S&P 500 ended up 0.2%.

Record results by chip maker Micron Technology provided a much-needed boost to investors amid lingering worries about the vast sums pumped into the AI sector in recent years, and when companies will see returns.

Traders are meanwhile awaiting Friday's US jobs data for clues on whether the Federal Reserve will follow up last month's interest rate hike, aimed at combatting elevated inflation, with another round of tightening in October.

The MRO work will be carried out at SAE's 50,000 square metre facility at Kuala Lumpur International Airport between 2027 and 2028.

MAG president and group chief executive officer Captain Nasaruddin A. Bakar said the acquisition would position the group to capture opportunities in the growing MRO market and meet rising third-party demand.
He said the deal would leverage Malaysia's cost-to-skill advantage and established engineering expertise, supporting the country's ambition to become a leading regional aerospace hub.
SAE complements MAB Engineering Services Sdn Bhd's existing capabilities through its A320 expertise, dedicated paint hangar and specialised component repair services.
